title: Will there be a major shift in cancer survival rates by 2030?
criteria: YES for a +20 percentage-point increase in five-year survival across all cancers by 2030; the market notes a data source clarification was still pending.
why: A 20-point change in five-year survival for all cancers is not a defined bound on the milestone's 80% ten-year net survival for solid tumors, nor does it establish metastatic cancer as manageable.

title: When will the average five-year survival rate of all cancers exceed 95%?
criteria: Date the average five-year survival rate for all cancers exceeds 95%; details on population and statistic are not exposed in the public page extract. Closes 2050-06-18.
why: The question uses a 95% five-year average across all cancers rather than 80% ten-year net survival for solid tumors, and those differently timed aggregate endpoints do not imply one another.

title: Will glioblastoma (an aggressive brain cancer) have a 5-year relative survival rate greater than 15% in the US in 2035?
criteria: YES if CBTRUS's 2035 report gives US glioblastoma five-year relative survival above 15% (currently cited baseline 6.9%); point estimate only.
why: This concerns one US brain-cancer subtype and a five-year threshold, which cannot bound 10-year survival across all solid tumors or demonstrate metastatic cancer management.

title: Will a therapy that substantially slows down or reverses the aging process in humans be developed before 2040?
criteria: Before 2040, a publicly documented, independently validated therapy must reduce average biological age by at least 10 years in 100+ people, improve at least two clinical endpoints/functions by at least 25%, and have an acceptable safety profile.
why: This is the closest aging candidate, but its composite biomarker definition and clinical-function improvements differ from the milestone's epigenetic-clock-plus-functional-biomarker validation and required reduction in age-related disease incidence.

title: Global CO2 Emissions Peak Year
criteria: Forecasts the year global CO2 emissions peak; public page discussion specifies CO2 including land-use change, not a three-year-confirmed all-greenhouse-gas peak.
why: The question forecasts a CO2 peak, whereas the milestone requires a major all-GHG inventory to show the peak at least three years back and the latest year 1% below it.

title: Will global carbon emissions from all sources peak before 2030?
criteria: YES if an annual emissions figure in 2025-2029 is below the prior year's, with resolution using official IEA or Global Carbon Project data by end-2030; description inconsistently calls this both all-source CO2-equivalent GHG and energy-related CO2.
why: Although its before-2030 threshold could precede confirmed peak status, its resolution text conflicts on CO2 versus all-GHG scope and lacks the milestone's three-year and 1% confirmation tests.

title: Will the world achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2060?
criteria: YES if worldwide carbon emissions are at most carbon removals by 2060 under globally accepted reporting standards.
why: It asks about carbon alone by 2060, not approximately-zero net anthropogenic all-GHG emissions in GWP100, so it does not provide a sound bound for the milestone.
